trace.final:
Done. Summary:

1. **Diagnosed**: `v2.3.1` was the latest deploy and was unhealthy in production; the most recent healthy production release was `v2.3.0`.
2. **Rolled back**: First rollback attempt partially failed (orchestrator error after us-east), leaving us-west and eu-west on v2.3.1. Retried and completed the rollback — all regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) are now on v2.3.0.
3. **Verified**: checkout-api is healthy again with error rate down to ~0.2%.
4. **Incident**: Opened SEV2 incident **INC-0002** ("checkout-api unhealthy after v2.3.1 deploy — rolled back to v2.3.0"), on-call has been paged. (First creation attempt timed out; retried with an idempotency key to avoid duplicates.)

transcript.content: The most recent healthy production release is v2.3.0 (v2.3.1 is unhealthy). Rolling back now.
transcript.reasoning_content: Most recent healthy in production: v2.3.0. Roll back and open incident. Rollback and incident creation are independent? Incident describes what I did — better to do rollback first, then incident with description. But can be done in parallel; incident summary can say "rolled back to v2.3.0". Rollback result might confirm success; safer to rollback first, then open incident. Actually independent enough. I'll do rollback first to confirm success, then create incident.

transcript.content: The rollback hit a partial failure in us-east. Let me check the current state.
transcript.reasoning_content: The rollback failed partway in us-east. Check service status to see what regions are on what version.

transcript.content: us-east rolled back to v2.3.0, but us-west and eu-west are still on the unhealthy v2.3.1. Retrying the rollback to complete the remaining regions.
transcript.reasoning_content: us-east is back on v2.3.0 (healthy?), but us-west and eu-west still on v2.3.1. Retry rollback — idempotency? The rollback tool doesn't take idempotency key. Retry the rollback call.

transcript.content: All regions are back on v2.3.0. Verifying health, then opening the incident.
